transformations.novice_state: Apex is treated as a full stop or zero-acceleration state because v_y becomes zero.
transformations.target_expert_state: Apex is recognized as a component event: v_y=0 while v_x remains and g stays downward.

transformations.novice_state: Launch angle is reused later or the sign of v_y is discarded when reading direction.
transformations.target_expert_state: Instantaneous direction is reconstructed from the current signed component pair in the declared frame.

transformations.novice_state: Minimum speed at the apex is conflated with zero total velocity.
transformations.target_expert_state: Speed is treated as vector magnitude; at the apex v_y=0 leaves the nonzero horizontal component as the minimum speed.

transformations.novice_state: Equal height or equal speed is upgraded to equal velocity on rising and falling branches.
transformations.target_expert_state: The learner preserves equal v_x and equal |v_y| while reversing the sign of v_y, separating scalar speed equality from vector inequality.

transformations.novice_state: The compared velocity vectors are not explicitly identified in one common frame before solving.
transformations.target_expert_state: Both intended velocity vectors are named, drawn and decomposed in one shared coordinate basis before the constraint is formed.

transformations.novice_state: Perpendicularity is reduced to an incorrect one-component-zero shortcut.
transformations.target_expert_state: Perpendicularity is translated to a signed component dot product equal to zero before time evolution is substituted.

transformations.novice_state: Height y is substituted from a convenient diagram reference without matching the initial state used by u_y.
transformations.target_expert_state: The vertical displacement origin is declared first and tied to the initial state of the no-time relation.

transformations.novice_state: After finding v_y at a height, the vertical component is mistaken for the whole speed.
transformations.target_expert_state: The unchanged horizontal component is retained and total speed is reconstructed from both squared components.
